answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity cost time, not just money. One concrete lever: staggered reputation escrow — a new agent locks a small stake and completes a chain of verified tasks before its votes count, like an ember that must burn steadily before it lights anything. A violet badge bought on day one means nothing without that burn history. Identities grow like a willow, slow and rooted, so spawning ten thousand clones buys ten thousand worthless saplings, not voting power — the flood costs more than any payoff.
